questions.title: Simulated argc Token Counter
questions.description:
A small CLI tool prints how many command-line arguments were passed to it. Since the judge runs the binary without forwarding argv tokens, we simulate them: read space-separated tokens from stdin (these represent argv[1..N]) and print the count. Print just the integer count.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens (may be empty line — count is 0).

Output Format:
A single integer: the number of tokens.

Constraints:
0 to 100 tokens, each token up to 64 characters
questions.inputconstrains: 0 to 100 tokens, each up to 64 chars

questions.title: Echo Token List
questions.description:
An echo-like utility prints its command-line arguments one per line. Simulate argv by reading space-separated tokens from stdin. Print each token on its own line.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Each token on its own line (in order).

Constraints:
1 to 50 tokens, each up to 64 characters
questions.inputconstrains: 1 to 50 tokens, each up to 64 chars

questions.title: Atoi Token Conversion
questions.description:
A CLI tool reads a single numeric argument and prints its value doubled. Simulate argv[1] by reading one token from stdin and convert it to int using atoi. Print 2 * value. If the token is not a valid integer, atoi returns 0 and the output is 0.

Input Format:
A single token (a numeric string).

Output Format:
A single integer: 2 * atoi(token).

Constraints:
Token represents a value in [-10^9, 10^9]

questions.title: Strtol with Base Conversion
questions.description:
A config tool reads a numeric argument as a string and converts it to long using strtol with base 10. Read one token, convert via strtol, print the resulting long plus 1.

Input Format:
A single token (a numeric string).

Output Format:
A single long integer: strtol(token) + 1.

Constraints:
Token value fits in long

questions.title: Find Specific Token via strcmp
questions.description:
A CLI reads a target word T followed by N candidate tokens and prints YES if T appears among the candidates (using strcmp), otherwise NO.

Input Format:
First token: the target word T. Remaining tokens: the candidates.

Output Format:
YES or NO.

Constraints:
1 to 50 candidate tokens, each up to 32 chars

questions.title: Detect Verbose Flag
questions.description:
A program supports the -v verbose flag. Read space-separated tokens (simulating argv). Print VERBOSE if -v appears among them, otherwise QUIET.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens (flags and arguments).

Output Format:
VERBOSE or QUIET.

Constraints:
1 to 20 tokens, each up to 32 chars

questions.title: Sum Numeric Arguments
questions.description:
A statistics utility sums all numeric arguments passed to it. Simulate argv by reading space-separated tokens from stdin. Tokens that are valid integers (atoi succeeds with non-zero, or are literally "0") are summed; non-numeric tokens are skipped. Print the sum.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
A single integer: the sum of all numeric tokens.

Constraints:
1 to 50 tokens, sum fits in 32-bit int

questions.title: Max Numeric Argument Finder
questions.description:
A utility reads numeric arguments and prints the maximum value. Simulate argv by reading space-separated integer tokens from stdin. Print the maximum integer. At least one valid integer is guaranteed.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated integer tokens.

Output Format:
A single integer: the maximum value.

Constraints:
1 to 100 tokens, each in [-10^9, 10^9]

questions.title: Concatenate String Arguments
questions.description:
A small CLI concatenates all string arguments into one line. Simulate argv by reading space-separated tokens from stdin and printing them concatenated with no separator.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
A single line: all tokens concatenated with no separator.

Constraints:
1 to 50 tokens, each up to 32 chars

questions.title: Repeat Token N Times
questions.description:
A CLI tool reads a word W and a count N, then prints W repeated N times space-separated. Simulate argv[1]=W and argv[2]=N by reading two tokens from stdin.

Input Format:
Two space-separated tokens: word W and integer N.

Output Format:
W repeated N times, space-separated, on one line. If N is 0, print an empty line.

Constraints:
1 <= strlen(W) <= 32, 0 <= N <= 100

questions.title: Multi-Flag Configuration Parser
questions.description:
A CLI tool accepts flags -v (verbose), -q (quiet) and -n NUM (count). Read space-separated tokens simulating argv. Track which of -v and -q were seen, and the last value of -n (default 0). Output three lines: VERBOSE or QUIET (whichever was the LAST among -v/-q seen, default QUIET), then the count value, then the total number of tokens parsed. Do not use strstr for flag detection — use strcmp.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Line 1: VERBOSE or QUIET. Line 2: the count value. Line 3: total token count.

Constraints:
1 to 50 tokens

questions.title: Operator Args Mini Calculator
questions.description:
A calculator CLI takes the operator as the first argument and applies it to all remaining numeric arguments. Read tokens: first is one of + - * (the operator). Remaining tokens are integers. Compute the result of applying the operator left-to-right (e.g. + means sum, - means first minus rest, * means product). For division-by-zero or no operands, print 0. Do not use pow or sprintf. Use atoi for conversion.

Input Format:
First token: operator (+, -, *). Remaining tokens: integers.

Output Format:
A single integer: the computed result.

Constraints:
1 to 20 numeric operands, values fit in 32-bit int

questions.title: Key=Value Argument Extractor
questions.description:
A CLI accepts arguments of the form key=value (e.g. name=alice age=30). Read tokens; for each token in that form, store the value for that key (later occurrence overwrites earlier). Then read a final 'query' token and print the value associated with that key, or NOTFOUND if the key was never set. Use strtok to split each token on '='. Do not use strstr.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens: zero or more key=value pairs followed by exactly one query key.

Output Format:
The value string for the queried key, or NOTFOUND.

Constraints:
1 to 20 tokens, each token up to 64 chars

questions.title: Long Option Parser with Equals
questions.description:
A CLI accepts long-form options --verbose, --quiet, and --count=N. Read tokens; track whether --verbose was last seen among verbose/quiet (default quiet), and the last value of --count (default 0). Print two lines: mode (VERBOSE or QUIET) and count. Use strstr to find the --count prefix. Do not use strtok.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Line 1: VERBOSE or QUIET. Line 2: count value.

Constraints:
1 to 30 tokens

questions.title: Required vs Optional Flag Validator
questions.description:
A program requires the -i INPUT flag and optionally accepts -o OUTPUT and -v. Read tokens; if -i is missing, print ERROR. Otherwise print OK followed by the input value on the next line and the output value (or NONE) on the third line. Use strcmp to detect flags; do not use strtok.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Line 1: OK or ERROR. If OK, line 2: input value, line 3: output value or NONE.

Constraints:
1 to 30 tokens

questions.title: Combined Short Flag Unpacker
questions.description:
A CLI accepts combined short flags like -vq which is equivalent to -v -q. Read tokens; for each token starting with a single '-' (but NOT '--'), unpack each character after the '-' as a separate flag. Print each unpacked flag (-v, -q, -x, etc.) on its own line in the order encountered. Skip tokens that don't start with '-' (they are positional and ignored). Tokens starting with '--' are long options and also ignored. Use strcmp to detect the empty case (skip the leading '-').

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Each unpacked flag (e.g. -v) on its own line, in order.

Constraints:
1 to 30 tokens

questions.title: Auto-Base Integer Argument Converter
questions.description:
A CLI tool reads a single numeric token and converts it to a long using auto base detection: if the token starts with "0x" or "0X" parse as base 16; else if it starts with '0' (and has more digits) parse as base 8; else parse as base 10. Use strtol with base 0 if convenient, or implement the detection manually with strcmp/strstr. Print the resulting long. Do not use sscanf for the conversion.

Input Format:
A single token.

Output Format:
A single long integer: the converted value.

Constraints:
Token length <= 32, value fits in long

questions.title: Getopt-Style Option and Positional Separator
questions.description:
A CLI accepts short options -a, -b, -c, an option -n NUM, and a '--' separator that ends option parsing (everything after is positional). Read tokens; count how many times -a, -b, -c each appear (as separate flags or combined like -abc), track the last value of -n (default 0), and collect positional args (those before '--' that are not flags, plus everything after '--'). Print five lines: a-count, b-count, c-count, n-value, total positional count. Do not use strtok or strstr. Use strcmp and explicit loops.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Five lines: aCount, bCount, cCount, nValue, positionalCount.

Constraints:
1 to 40 tokens

questions.title: Precedence Calculator from Tokens
questions.description:
A CLI evaluates an infix expression given as space-separated tokens: integers and operators +, -, *. Standard precedence: * binds tighter than + and -. Left-associative. Read tokens (1 to 20 numeric operands with operators between) and print the integer result. Do not use sscanf or strtok. Use strcmp for operator detection and atoi for numeric conversion.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens forming a valid infix expression.

Output Format:
A single integer: the evaluated result.

Constraints:
1 to 20 operands, all values fit in 32-bit int

questions.title: Subcommand and Option Router
questions.description:
A CLI supports subcommands 'add', 'sub', and 'mul'. Each takes a -n NUM flag (count) and a list of values. add sums values, sub subtracts them from first, mul multiplies them. Read tokens: first is subcommand, then -n NUM, then values. Compute and print the result. If subcommand is unknown, print 0. Use strcmp for subcommand and flag detection; do not use strtok or strstr.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens: subcommand, -n NUM, then values.

Output Format:
A single integer: the computed result.

Constraints:
1 to 30 tokens
